length_policy.policy: Two developed scenes of approximately 900 words each; the size of the fictional universe remains open.

title: The Last Gate of the Shore
retrieval_query: Iliad heroic honor divine gift competing authority mortal vulnerability supplication war
genre: Epic historical fiction with original characters and ancient material obligations.
reader_experience: Close material attention, household urgency, curiosity and unease when an investigation imposes a concrete cost.
pov: Third-person past tense with one primary focal character per scene. No direct or quoted dialogue. Indirect reports, narrated offers, refusals, promises and commitments are explicitly permitted. No invocation or direct address.
tone_mood: Grave and martial, with tenderness in concrete duties; wonder before divine craft and unease beneath victory. No modern sarcasm or action-film triumphalism.
sensory_detail: Concrete material detail perceived through ancient experience: bronze, sea, wool, ash, labor, bodies and weather.
ending_tendency: Leave consequential open threads; the world has no predetermined final ending.
premise: Write two developed, causally connected scenes on the storm-damaged Achaean shore. Twelve named people have distinct duties, private knowledge, tools and debts, but only the planned participants act on-page. Thestor must spend one of his two single-use gate seals to get a household through the inner gate. Lyra must later spend the remaining seal on the outer barrier and solve a powerless latch through the red release pin she actually possesses. Costs and knowledge must carry between scenes through actual witnessed events. Make each bargain and rescue emotionally specific; avoid a mechanical inventory recital. The Trojan War remains unresolved.

keywords.term: divine gift with an unequally distributed cost
loyalty to comrades versus obedience to a king

reference_policy: Pin Iliad analysis work_136 as primary. Supplement only when it serves an actual gap. This is alternate continuity, not an episode narrated by Homer. Analyses alone are not authority for exact historical facts; preserve source limitations. No modern translation passages.

preserve: Recognizable principal relationships and ancient social values
Hector and Achilles alive in this installment
adaptation.divergence: Future background only: divine firearms may later enter this alternate continuity. This practice scene reveals only a damaged unknown object and cannot acquire or operate a weapon.
adaptation.interpretation: Strong source influence and pinned source selection; strength is guidance, not a measured borrowed percentage.

style.narrator: Third-person past-tense epic narrator, with a primary focal character per scene. The narrator may supply another character’s history or inner attention in a clearly separated paragraph, but this never grants other characters private knowledge. No dialogue, quoted speech, first-person narrator, invocation or direct address. Narrate offers and commitments briefly and show their consequences.
style.register: Concrete, grave, musical ancient epic in intelligible English. Use material acts, reciprocal obligation, shame and rank; no stock modern cinematic gestures.
wording: Recurring epithets at meaningful moments; avoid attaching one to every name.
Period-fitting names: unfamiliar iron object, then iron tubes or fire-bearing tubes; keep naming consistent. No modern military vocabulary.
Ancient measures and experiences; no modern technical or psychological vocabulary.
Contemporary English grammar shaped by ancient epic; no indiscriminate thee/thou or faux-biblical filler.
Gods and human motives intertwine, while choices retain consequences.
No quotation or close reproduction of a modern translation.

figurative_language.guidance: Roughly one extended comparison per scene when earned, no mandatory quota. Let its image develop before returning to action. No modern image domains or continuous ornament.

style.interiority: Selective focalized thought tied to a practical choice, remembered obligation or fear of a specific loss; no abstract emotional labels.
style.dialogue: No direct/quoted speech. Indirect narrated offers and refusals are permitted, but do not repeat an already completed negotiation.
style.explanation: Cut explanations that merely restate legible action. Preserve purposeful epic repetition, ceremonial speech, lyricism and similes.

world_rules: Exactly two single-use bronze gate seals exist at the opening; spending one destroys it permanently.
One seal opens the inner gate once; a second seal opens the outer barrier once.
No replacement seals, duplicate seals, supernatural refunds or offstage resupply exist.
Only Thestor and Lyra know the opening seal count until an actual disclosure.
A person knows private information only after a witnessed disclosure or discovery.
Author knowledge, future scene plans and another character's private memory are not shared knowledge.
Travel between the gate and quay takes physical effort and cannot be instantaneous.
The flooded low path remains impassable during this episode.
The collapsed western quay cannot suddenly serve as a safe landing.
The eastern gate is the only usable evacuation route.
The red release pin is held by Lyra at opening; track its custody.
The red pin opens only the powerless outer latch; it cannot create resources or open the inner gate.
Any tool transfer must happen on-page or be explicitly reported by an accountable witness.
The departure roster exists on one tablet; no unexplained copy can solve a dispute.
There are three intact mooring ropes at the opening; track any expenditure or damage.
The first relief chest contains six linen rolls; expenditure reduces that count.
Four unopened barley sacks exist at the grain shed; no hidden extra store appears.
Neris alone knows the second relief chest was never loaded; others cannot use that secret without learning it.
A belief that the quay will hold is uncertain, not a forecast guaranteed by narration.
A witnessed debt may change through explicit payment, release or a new agreement; preserve its history.
A confirmed death cannot be reversed; there are no substitutes, clones or concealed survivals.
An injury, lost tool, abandoned load or broken promise has consequences in later scenes.
Divine intervention cannot cancel an established cost, grant omniscience or refund a spent seal.
Keep ancient material perception, named social obligations and distinct character aims; no modern jargon or mechanical status summaries.

world_design.setting: Storm-damaged Achaean harbor and its two gates.
world_design.technology: Bronze seals, wax tablets, rope, wooden gates; no modern machinery.
world_design.institutions: A shore commander, gate warden and labor debts witnessed on a public tally.
world_design.physical_systems: A rising tide and a powerless outer latch; costs are material.
world_design.deadlines: Evacuation must precede the next high-water mark.

plot_design.central_question: Can reciprocal obligations move a household before the harbor closes?
causal_dependencies: The first seal is spent in scene one; only the actual remainder may reach scene two.
The red pin remains a specific custody-bound tool, not a magic rescue.

subplots.question: Will she risk the borrowed pin?
subplots.intersection: The final latch requires the pin she promised to return.
subplots.removal_cost: Without the promise her last choice has no personal cost.

alternatives_and_costs: Keep the seals and abandon a household, or spend them and lose the protection of controlled access.

scene_designs.setting: The tide pushes scraps of wreckage against a gate crowded by households.
scene_designs.dramatic_function: Spend exactly one seal to open the inner gate and secure a household passage.
scene_designs.development: Thestor and Odysseus reach one costly witnessed agreement; Thestor spends one seal and visibly transfers the remaining single unused seal to Lyra.
scene_designs.restrictions: Do not open the outer barrier, spend the second seal, reveal Neris's secret or use Lyra's red pin yet.
scene_designs.choice_and_consequence: The household passes the inner gate; one irreversible seal expenditure and explicit custody transfer change the next scene.

scene_designs.location: The outer barrier and eastern quay
scene_designs.setting: The remaining boat strains against its ropes as water nears the white marker.
scene_designs.time: After the household reaches the outer barrier
scene_designs.dramatic_function: Spend the remaining seal once, then land the household through a powerless outer latch.
scene_designs.development: Lyra receives only what actually arrived from scene one, spends the last seal on the barrier, and uses her own red release pin at the powerless latch at a concrete personal cost. Briseis and Leontes have competing duties.
scene_designs.restrictions: No reset of seals or inventory; do not replay the first bargain, reveal Neris's secret, use the collapsed quay, add power, or give the red pin a new function.
scene_designs.choice_and_consequence: The household boards or lands through an earned physical solution, both seals remain spent, and an obligation remains meaningful.

must_avoid: Modern diction or modern psychological frameworks.
Modern translation quotation or close imitation of a particular translation.
Handwaved acquisition, immediate complete understanding, unlimited ammunition.
Repeated discovery scenes, decorative speeches without competing aims.
Explaining already legible gestures or declaring that war changed forever.
Removing ceremonial speech, earned similes or purposeful epic repetition merely to modernize prose.
Resolving the whole Trojan War or killing Hector or Achilles.

chapter_contract.arc: Consequential actions change a persistent world without a predetermined ending.
chapter_contract.continuity: Preserve custody, time, condition, obligations and individual knowledge.
chapter_contract.ending: An episode can end with a consequential open thread; no forced resolution.

quality_contract: No direct or quoted dialogue; indirect narration of offers and commitments is explicitly permitted.
Maintain all actual costs, witnesses, individual knowledge and resource custody between scenes.
Each scene must add a new consequential action, not replay the earlier bargain or rescue.
Use vivid ancient material detail, character agency, subtext and a costly choice; never recite an inventory.
Only planned participants must appear; the remaining cast still has persistent memories and obligations.
chapter_arcs: A household seeks passage. Storm damage exposes a troubling object; choosing to investigate costs time or wages. No completed decipherment, divine visit, expedition or weapon acquisition.
